question: The original Rules of Procedure (RoP) of the High-Level Expert Group on access to data for effective law enforcement (HLG) of 4 October 20231 provided for significantly more transparency than the subsequently changed rules of 22 January 2024 do2. EDRi has commented that the HLG does not meet ‘EU standards of transparency, fairness and accountability.’3 1.
Why, on what legal basis and under whose responsibility were the original RoP for the HLG subsequently modified?
When will the Commission make available ‘the agendas, the minutes and the participants’ submissions’ of the HLG, in accordance with the current rules?
For how long will the HLG exist, and when will it adopt findings, conclusions or recommendations?
answer: The High-Level Group on access to data for effective law enforcement was launched in June 2023 in order to explore challenges that law enforcement practitioners in the EU face in their daily work in connection with access to data and potential solutions to overcome them, with the aim of ensuring the availability of effective law enforcement tools to fight crime and maintain public security in the digital age.

The Group shall exist until 31 December 2024 and will submit its concluding report prior to this date. The Group adopted its rules of procedure, which ensure an equivalent degree of transparency to the one applicable to Commission expert groups (4).

The rules of procedure were modified and adopted in accordance with Article 9 of Commission Decision C (2023)3647 (5) to reflect the fact that the group is not required to be registered in the register of Commission expert groups. Point 12 of the rules stipulates that the Commission services (Directorate General for Migration and Home Affairs) will make available relevant documents on a dedicated website.

Access to documents is granted in line with the applicable rules laid down in Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 (6), notably not to undermine the protection of a public or private interest as defined in Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.
